I just retested it with 4.4.1, and the behaviour was the same.

Body tracking on the quest doesn't work with trackers, it will update skeleton data and work through the body tracking system in Godot which we support through the vendor plugin.

OpenXR doesn't support additional trackers outside of the [HTC vive tracker extension](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenXR/specs/1.1/html/xrspec.html#XR_HTCX_vive_tracker_interaction) which we do have support for.
The question is whether the WiVrn runtime supports this. Quest does not.

It's possible that certain tracker solutions have their own OpenXR layers to add functionality but if this is so, a plugin will need to be created implementing the related extensions.

Thanks for the info. I'm a bit confused, however, about the point of having additional trackers provided by WiVRn, then.

I briefly looked at WiVRn's client code and found this:
https://github.com/WiVRn/WiVRn/blob/6d0cc606265d22140f0b7ad3488b49544a533b4b/client/xr/fb_body_tracker.h

Looks like they have a body tracker support for Vive, Pico, and Meta ('FB'). In that case, can I assume that the "generic tracker" I see is just how WiVRn represents Meta Quest's body trackers, which will be accessible through Meta's [OpenXR extension](https://developers.meta.com/horizon/documentation/native/android/move-body-tracking/) once Godot adds support for it?

> WiVRn represents Meta Quest's body trackers, which will be accessible through Meta's [OpenXR extension](https://developers.meta.com/horizon/documentation/native/android/move-body-tracking/) once Godot adds support for it?

We do have support for Meta's body trackers, but you need to use the [godot_openxr_vendors](https://github.com/GodotVR/godot_openxr_vendors) extension. You can try the [body tracking sample](https://godotengine.org/asset-library/asset/3385) from the asset library

If you do give it a try, please report back if that works or not!

Thanks! I totally missed the vendor extension.

However, it doesn't seem to work on WiVRn for some reason. When I download and run the sample project, the avatar remains still although I can move around in the game environment.

I also tried to install the addon to my project and tried the test, but it still reports only 3 basic trackers. I double checked that I have enabled the body tracking support both in WiVRn, and Godot (the settings appeared after I installed the extension).

By the way, I just found a seemingly related issue from WiVRn:
https://github.com/WiVRn/WiVRn/issues/421

Perhaps, it could be a limitation on WiVRn's end?

> it doesn't seem to work on WiVRn for some reason

WiVRn uses the `MNDX_xdev_space` extension for generic trackers. This is an unregistered extension (and is mostly a hack to let tools like `xrizer` or `OpenComposite` forward those trackers to OpenVR to unblock FBT support *at all* while we wait for a better extension to come around, which is tricky to design, and the HTCX one is very problematic). I would personally highly recommend applications/libraries abstain from supporting xdev_space due to it's design limitations (it returns ALL devices, including head/hands, with *no* way to tell what is a tracker and what is not a tracker, and also has fingerprinting risks).

That is the only way WiVRn currently exposes these generic trackers. Monado supports these FB body tracking extensions, but generic trackers don't automatically map to it (since that would require IK which is not implemented).  https://github.com/WiVRn/WiVRn/issues/421 is about forwarding that data as both generic trackers *and* as proper data sources for the facebook body tracking extensions.

Ah, is the `MNDX_xdev_space` extension the one referred to in [this proposal](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13284)?

I've had some trouble tracking down documentation for it, but this appears to be the source code for it in Monado:

https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/monado/monado/-/blob/main/src/xrt/state_trackers/oxr/oxr_api_xdev.c?ref_type=heads

> Ah, is the `MNDX_xdev_space` extension the one referred to in [this proposal](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13284)?
> 
> I've had some trouble tracking down documentation for it, but this appears to be the source code for it in Monado:
> 
> [gitlab.freedesktop.org/monado/monado/-/blob/main/src/xrt/state_trackers/oxr/oxr_api_xdev.c?ref_type=heads](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/monado/monado/-/blob/main/src/xrt/state_trackers/oxr/oxr_api_xdev.c?ref_type=heads)

There's little-to-no documentation, but you can find the official header [here](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/monado/monado/-/blob/main/src/external/openxr_includes/openxr/XR_MNDX_xdev_space.h?ref_type=heads) and an example usage app [here](https://gitlab.com/caszu/OpenOVR/-/blob/openxr/DrvOpenXR/XrBackend.cpp#L993). However as I stated before, the extension returns all devices on the system, with no way to distinguish between what's a tracker and what's some other "xdev", it's leaking internal implementation details quite strongly, like the fact your HMD could be as many as 5 xdevs, so will enumerate 5 times.

Applications like OpenComposite/xrizer will use some basic heuristics like "does it contain the word `tracke`" which has both false positives *and* false negatives, so it's really un-ideal. I'd argue a generic middleware like Godot should avoid it.

I've been working with upstream Monado the past few months to try to design a new arbitrary tracker extension we _could_ register upstream, but it's been a long process and no side is *suuper* happy with what I've been able to come up with, because it's either leaking implementation details, too far from what OpenXR tries to be, or if it fits both of the first criteria, it doesn't cover some obvious usecase which is needed by end users (and is *already* possible and in active use with OpenVR).

The HTCX extension is fundamentally broken in that infinite arbitrary trackers (no defined role) require rebooting the *entire* OpenXR session to bind to, so Monado has made the conscious decision not to support it as of now, due to it's flaws.
